newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's PUMA issues A$500 mln bond.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's PUMA issues A$500 mln bond.

text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd's securitisation arm PUMA said on Tuesday it has issued a A$500 million four tranche domestic bond issue, with the pricing due on or before Friday, June 6.
The issue, to be known as PUMA Masterfund P-6, Series B, would be settled on June 13.
Tranche 1-F, which has a fixed coupon until April 15 2000, will have a face value of A$315 million and is fungible with Masterfund P-6 Series A tranche 1-F.
It will therefore carry a coupon of 6.9 percent and will be priced against the Commonwealth Government April 2000 bond.
The other tranches will be floating rate transactions.
Tranche 2 will have a face value of A$135 million and has an average expected life of seven years.

Tranche 3 will have a face value of A$23 million and an average expected life of 7.3 years, while tranche 4, which is a subordinated tranche, will have a face value of A$27 million and also have an average expected life of 7.3 years.
Tranches one to three are expected to be rated AAA/Aaa by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service and Tranche four is expected to be rated AA minus by S&P.
A large portion of the funds raised from this issue woul be used to finance home loans secured through PUMA's strategic partner Aussie Home Loans, said PUMA Managing Director, Tony Gill.

Gill said PUMA Masterfund P-6, Series B will be PUMA's third issue for calendar 1997, taking total issuance for the year to date to over $1.9 billion, which includes its $912 million debut Euro issue launched in March.

"We expect to achieve competitive pricing on these bonds, based on PUMA's strong name in the marketplace, the fungibility of the fixed rate tranche and the structural enhancements built into PUMA issues," Gill said.
"These enhancements are designed to minimise some of the risk home by investors by providing investors with greater certainty over their cash flows," Gill added.
Gill said these features include a substitution period and issuer call dates with margin compensation kickers.
"These features are incorporated into all PUMA principal and interest bonds but they are not always built into all mortgage backed issues," Gill added.
